mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has drifted downward for three of the last four weeks (-13.0, -10.1, -12.0, -12.6), indicating a persistent negative momentum in discretionary foot traffic. This autocorrelated trend is expected to persist without an external shock, pulling the next 4-week mean below the current 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -10.1 at t-2w to -12.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the next 4-week RETAIL_REC mean rises above the current 4-week mean despite no intervening recovery in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp single-week plunge in WORKPLACES mobility (from -8.0 to -16.1 at t-1w) signals an abrupt tightening of workplace-related restrictions or advisories. Such tightening typically precedes or coincides with reduced retail and recreation visits as general mobility caution spreads, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean falls below -15 relative to baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped to -16.1 at t-1w before partially recovering to -6.6
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to decline (or rises) in the two weeks following a WORKPLACES reading below -15, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL time (consistently +10 to +13 above baseline) combined with persistently depressed TRANSIT (around -18 to -20) jointly indicate sustained risk-averse, stay-home behavior. The interaction of these two signals compounds to suppress discretionary outings more than either series alone would predict, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained above +10 all four weeks while TRANSIT stayed below -17
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated and TRANSIT staying depressed, the compounding behavioral interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated sharply in the latest week (-16.7, the lowest of the four-week window), consistent with Singapore's inter-monsoon season bringing more frequent rain that discourages outdoor park visits. As outdoor leisure becomes less attractive, some of that activity is expected to substitute into indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -10.9 at t-2w to -16.7 at t-0w
regime_hint: inter-monsoon seasonal transition with increased rainfall
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat while PARKS keeps falling, the outdoor-to-indoor substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has oscillated near multi-week lows, touching -20.4 at t-1w. When transit usage falls below a critical threshold, it reflects reduced willingness to travel for non-essential purposes, which should translate almost immediately into lower retail and recreation visits in the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT recorded -20.1 at t-3w and -20.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following a TRANSIT reading below -20, the short-horizon threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed persistently positive (+6 to +7) while RETAIL_REC remains deeply negative, suggesting households are substituting discretionary shopping trips with essential-only errands. The interaction of rising essential-trip share and flat discretionary mobility signals a durable behavioral reallocation that should keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed between +6.3 and +7.1 for three weeks while RETAIL_REC stayed below -10
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises toward baseline even as GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, the essential-substitution interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The large week-to-week swing in WORKPLACES (-8.0 to -16.1 to -6.6) alongside persistently high RESIDENTIAL readings suggests an unstable policy regime with intermittent tightening of movement restrictions. In such a regime, renewed caution from policy flip-flopping is expected to keep RETAIL_REC depressed for the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly swing exceeds 7 points while RESIDENTIAL remains above +10
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES swung from -8.0 to -16.1 and back to -6.6 while RESIDENTIAL stayed above +10 throughout
regime_hint: renewed restriction tightening regime with policy volatility
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises despite continued WORKPLACES volatility and elevated RESIDENTIAL, the policy-instability regime hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The steady rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside stabilizing RETAIL_REC in the most recent week may reflect early pre-festive-season stocking behavior ahead of an upcoming holiday period, which historically front-loads retail spending and lifts RETAIL_REC in the following weeks as shoppers increase discretionary purchases.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained elevated near +6 to +7 while RETAIL_REC stabilized around -12 to -13 in the latest two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following stable-to-rising GROCERY_PHARM readings, the pre-festive front-loading hypothesis is falsified.
